TL;DR: Great game, not incredibly easy if you want to complete all the challenges on each level, co-op is amazing.

The not-so-long version:

- The gameplay is great, it's what we already know from Rollercoaster Tycoon and Planet Coaster, very polished, and I haven't encountered any noticeable bugs.
- The co-op to me gives the game huge advantage over Planet Coaster, and much better than the afterthought that was the co-op on Planet Coaster 2 "Franchises", since you can play the whole campaign with friends.
- It's simple on the surface but each mechanic has its depth, so you can play it casually but if you want to get into it, it doesn't disappoint and rewards you for it.
- For the price this is an amazing deal, either solo or with friends, to me this is the actual successor to Rollercoaster Tycoon.

If you grew up playing RCT 1/2, this game will hit you right in the childhood.

Parkitect perfectly captures the magic that made those games special. The grid-based building, the coaster design, the guests wandering around your park, the music, the management… it all feels like a modern love letter to the classic theme park games many of us spent hundreds of hours on growing up.

What I love most is that it doesn't try to reinvent the formula, it builds on it!

Pros:

- Feels like the true spiritual successor to RCT with updated ease of life tools.
- Classic management gameplay that’s easy to learn but hard to master. 
- Clean, colourful art style that ages really well.
- Very fun campaign, while having the option to sandbox.
- Multiplayer! How we would've loved this when we played RCT many years ago!
- Workshop support adds endless content for us to delve into.

Cons:

- If you never liked classic park management games, this probably won’t change your mind.
- If you prefer extremely deep and complex park management systems, this may feel a little lighter. That said, I personally find it far more fun and enjoyable than Planet Coaster because of this. RCT style.

Extra detail that makes it special:
The backstage logistics system (staff paths, supply depots, deliveries etc.) adds a layer of management that the old RCT games never had, but it fits perfectly for an extra challenge.

Overall:
If RollerCoaster Tycoon was your childhood, Parkitect feels like coming home. It captures that same feeling of spending hours building the perfect park, tweaking coaster layouts, and watching guests enjoy something you created.

Final Score: 10/10 🎢
